item.title: #3530051: Update `ComponentAudit::getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingComponent()` to support component versions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +23/−1 · php +23/−1
  • Discussion: #3530051 · 2 contributors · 12 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 2 contributors

Summary

Canvas (formerly Experience Builder) can now ask which config entities, such as pattern or page region entities, depend on particular versions of a Component, not just on the Component as a whole. The goal is to support later work on pruning unused Component versions (#3530097). Calls that don't pass versions behave as before. This describes the merge request diff, which is a proposal.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ComponentAudit::getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingComponent() accepts an optional array $version_ids = [] to restrict results to config entities using those Component versions.

Technical details

The method signature becomes getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingComponent(ComponentInterface $component, string $config_entity_type_id, array $version_ids = []). It mirrors the version-aware getContentRevisionsUsingComponent(). When $version_ids is non-empty, the dependents found through the config dependency manager are filtered further. Each dependent is loaded. It is kept only if it implements VersionedConfigEntityInterface, one of the requested versions exists in getVersions(), and getVersionSpecificDependencies($version_id) for that version contains the Component's config dependency name. Dependents that are not versioned config entities are dropped when a version filter is given. With an empty array the original behavior is unchanged. The diff shows no test changes, and the author left the issue at "Needs work" so others could add tests.

item.title: #3592235: Workspaces PR 5: editor read path and Live writes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 26 files, +1039/−58 · php +698/−45 · js +333/−7 · md +7/−5 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 9a92022
  • Discussion: #3592235 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, the Canvas editor now works against the active workspace. Opening the editor with no active workspace switches to Main (when the user may view it). Drafts are read from the workspace, while page deletes, translation deletes and config translation override deletes act directly on Live. Deleting a page or translation that another workspace has staged changes for is refused with a 409 naming that workspace. Content create and status changes stay inside the workspace, and config entity writes through the Canvas config API still go to Live at once.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Permission change: Page delete access is now decided against Live (ApiContentControllers::deleteAccess()), so the delete link and route work while a workspace is active. Publish in tests needs edit any workspace.

Technical details

Core has no staged deletion and forbids deleting an entity Live has while a workspace is active. ApiContentControllers::delete() and ApiTranslationControllers::delete() therefore became instance methods that call WorkspaceAutoSave::assertNotLockedInAnotherWorkspace() and then wrap the delete in executeOutsideWorkspace() (from OptionalWorkspaceManagerTrait). The canvas.api.content.delete route swaps _entity_access for _custom_access: ApiContentControllers::deleteAccess, which checks delete access outside the workspace. The ::list() delete link uses the same check. The translation delete loads Live via loadLiveVersion(), removes the translation and saves outside the workspace. That save fires hook_entity_translation_delete(), which drops the translation from every workspace's staged copy. If the translation exists only in the active workspace's draft, it calls AutoSaveManager::deleteTranslation() instead. The two PHPStan ignores on $workspaceManager are removed now that it is read.

Route upcasting runs inside the workspace, so the upcast entity may be a staged revision. ApiLayoutController (layout GET and the label callback) and EntityFormController (AJAX POST rebuild) now call WorkspaceAutoSave::loadLiveVersion() when no auto-save data applies. In the layout GET, Live also becomes $original_entity, so isNew and hasUnsavedStatusChange are not computed against the staged revision. In the form rebuild, building from the staged revision would add extra rows to multi-value widgets. CanvasController::__invoke() loads the Main workspace (AutoSaveWorkspace::ID) and calls setActiveWorkspace() if none is active and the user has view access. The canvas_update_11201() guard still applies because $workspaceManager is nullable. ComponentInstanceForm now implements WorkspaceSafeFormInterface. Client side, brandKit.ts updateAutoSave now handles the returned autoSaves hash. Other UI service changes were not in the portion of the diff I read.

Several @todo Workspaces MR n: markers were added or retargeted. They cover the status default in ContentTemplate::createFromClientSide() (MR 9, templates are still created enabled), the lockedInWorkspace response key (MR 8), publish access (MR 7a) and whether Main stays active after leaving the editor (MR 16). The ADR text is updated: content create runs inside the workspace and templates are created enabled.

item.title: #3592234: Workspaces MR 4: component generation outside the workspace
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +386/−60 · php +383/−56 · yml +1 · txt +1 · md +1/−4
  • Diff: e61b234
  • Discussion: #3592234 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, Canvas now generates Component config entities outside the active workspace. Component config generated from code, such as block components, is written to Live. It no longer piles up as pending changes in each workspace. Switching workspaces also no longer triggers a cascade of component regeneration inside the workspace. Code components are the exception. They are config entities edited in Canvas, so their generated Component follows them into the active workspace. Publishing a workspace draft of a code component's Component now requires update access to the code component, meaning the administer code components permission.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ComponentSourceManager takes a new optional $workspaceManager constructor argument (@?workspaces.manager), and generated Components now save to Live unless their source sets discoveryReadsStagedConfig.
  • New API: New discoveryReadsStagedConfig property (default FALSE) on the ComponentSource plugin attribute, set TRUE on JsComponent.

Technical details

ComponentSourceManager::generateComponents() has a private $generating flag, set in a try/finally block. Saving Component config switches workspace context. That clears entity field definitions, which makes Layout Builder clear block plugin definitions. BlockManagerDecorator then calls back into generation, so nested calls return early. The finally block resets the flag after a failed pass.

The manager splits the source definitions in two. Sources whose definition has discoveryReadsStagedConfig TRUE are generated in the current workspace. All other sources are generated together in a single executeOutsideWorkspace() call, from the new OptionalWorkspaceManagerTrait. ComponentSourceManager gets an optional $workspaceManager constructor argument, wired as @?workspaces.manager in canvas.services.yml. The comment in the diff says it is NULL until a 1.x site has run canvas_update_11201().

The ComponentSource attribute gains a bool $discoveryReadsStagedConfig = FALSE property. JsComponent sets it to TRUE.

AutoSaveWorkspacePublishSubscriber no longer skips the access check for generated Components. The skip was previously inert and carried a @todo Workspaces MR 4. A new accessSubject() checks update access on the source JavaScriptComponent for JsComponent-sourced Components. It falls back to the Component itself if the code component is gone (ComponentNotFoundException).

The BlockComponent block settings subform class now also implements core's WorkspaceSafeFormInterface. Without it, core refuses to submit the form inside a workspace, so blockSubmit() was skipped. A kernel test showed this left multiplier at 0.

New and extended tests are ComponentSourceManagerWorkspaceTest, BlockComponentTest and WorkspaceAutoSaveStagingTest. The ADR text drops the sentence saying the block manager decorator regenerates only when the plugin ID set changed.

Upgrade

Custom ComponentSource plugins whose discovery reads workspace-staged config entities should opt in:

#[ComponentSource(
  // ...
  discoveryReadsStagedConfig: TRUE,
)]

Leaving the default (FALSE) generates the plugin's Component config against Live.

item.title: #3592275: Add a permission so non-admin users can view component folders
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +27/−2 · php +27/−2
  • Diff: c37da21
  • Discussion: #3592275 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Content creators who can use the Canvas editor but lack administer folders now see component folders (Library categories) in the component picker. Before, components showed up ungrouped and no folders were listed. Rename, update and delete still need administer folders. Sites that granted administer folders only so editors could browse folders can remove that grant.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Permission change: Users with Canvas UI access can now view folders without administer folders; create, update and delete still require administer folders.

Technical details

The Folder config entity used core's default EntityAccessControlHandler, so only users with administer folders passed view access. The picker's list endpoint filters out entities the user can't view, which dropped every folder for other editors. The access handler on Folder is now ContentCreatorVisibleCanvasConfigEntityAccessControlHandler, the same handler Component, Pattern and Color use. This is "Option B" from the issue. The proposed new view folders permission (Option A) was not added.

A new kernel test, FolderTest::testViewAccess(), covers this. A user with ContentTemplate::ADMIN_PERMISSION (a permission that grants Canvas UI access) can view and view label a folder, but not update or delete it. A user with no permissions cannot view it.

item.title: #3592281: Editor preview can start at the wrong position after page height changes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +4/−0 · css +4
  • Diff: 91b1d76
  • Discussion: #3592281 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, switching from a long page to a short page through the Pages panel could leave the top of the short page scrolled out of view. In the reported case it sat about 289px above the pane instead of about 50px below it. The preview now starts at its intended position after this switch.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is one CSS property, overflow-anchor: none, added to .editorPane (the scrollable pane that holds the preview). The editor sets this pane's scroll position itself. The issue's explanation is that the browser's scroll anchoring moved the scroll position when the preview shifted while the frame was catching up with a change in its size. Turning anchoring off stops the browser from adjusting the position on its own. The issue also reports a smaller, intermittent offset (about 58px instead of 50px) when loading a short page. It says a shared cause for the two symptoms was not confirmed, and the diff does not address that offset specifically.

item.title: #3592282: Fix Brand Kit color test flakiness caused by folder menu focus restoration
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +147/−15 · js +147/−15
  • Diff: 42bae7f
  • Discussion: #3592282 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In Canvas Brand Kit, choosing "Add color" from a color folder's menu could let the closing menu return focus to its trigger after the color popover had opened. If you typed into a field such as Alpha quickly, that late focus change blurred the field and could reset an invalid value, which re-enabled the Add button. The folder menu no longer takes focus back when it hands focus to the popover. Pressing Escape still returns focus to the menu trigger.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The Brand Kit colors section already used a suppressAutoFocusRef flag to stop the top-level dropdown's onCloseAutoFocus from restoring focus. The per-folder menus did not use it. The check is now a shared handleMenuCloseAutoFocus handler in BrandKitColorsSection. It calls preventDefault() when the flag is set, then resets the flag. The folder "Add color" menu item now sets suppressAutoFocusRef.current = true before opening the popover.

The handler is passed to the folder menus as a new optional onMenuCloseAutoFocus prop on FolderList. FolderList forwards it to SidebarFolder, which wires it to onCloseAutoFocus on both the dropdown and the context-menu UnifiedMenu.Content. Without the flag set, normal menu dismissal behaves as before.

A new Vitest spec for BrandKitColorsSection adds two tests. The first uses fake timers to enter an invalid Alpha (-0.5) before the menu's delayed focus return. It then asserts that the field keeps focus, the value stays, and the save button is disabled. The second asserts that Escape still returns focus to the menu trigger. The issue says this fixes the identified focus-related failure in brandKitColors.spec.ts, not every possible source of flakiness.

item.title: #3592279: Editor does not scroll to the top of the page preview on load
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +9/−9 · js +9/−9
  • Diff: 780a052
  • Discussion: #3592279 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

When the Canvas editor opens a page, it now reliably scrolls so the top of the preview, including the site header, is visible with a small gap above it. Before, some pages opened scrolled too far down, hiding the header, and short pages could open at the bottom.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The initial scroll position in EditorFrame.tsx was computed as (pane.scrollHeight - previewHeight) / 2 - 50. That assumes scrollHeight equals the frame padding plus the preview height. While the preview loads, content can briefly overflow the frame, so scrollHeight is inflated. In the issue's example at 1440×900, scrollHeight was 3026 px at computation time against 2409 px after load, so the editor scrolled to 979 px instead of 670 px.

The fix measures the preview's actual offset in the pane: scalingContainerRef top minus editorPaneRef top plus editorPaneRef.current.scrollTop. It then subtracts the 50 px gap. The horizontal position still comes from getHalfwayScrollPosition.

item.title: #3592277: Reuse the session's CSRF token instead of fetching it before every mutation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +129/−18 · js +129/−18
  • Diff: 4b881e2
  • Discussion: #3592277 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The Canvas editor no longer requests a new CSRF token from /session/token before every save. It fetches the token once while the editor loads and reuses it. The issue reports a 330–600 ms delay before each component PATCH on a dev site under load, and a first PATCH sent 21 ms after the edit with the change. If the session changes, for example after logging out and back in from another tab, a rejected save fetches a fresh token and is sent once more.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

fetchCsrfToken() in ui/src/utils/csrf.ts now keeps a per-base-URL Map of token promises. Concurrent callers share one in-flight request. A failed fetch removes its own entry, so failures are not cached. A new forgetCsrfToken(baseUrl) clears the entry so the next call fetches a new token.

ui/src/main.tsx calls fetchCsrfToken() at startup, so the first mutation reuses that request. In rawBaseQuery (ui/src/services/baseQuery.ts), a mutation that returns a 403 calls forgetCsrfToken() and is retried once. fetchAssertion in useHeadlessDraftSession.ts does the same drop-and-retry-once for its POST. The issue's reasoning for retrying is that Drupal rejects stale-token requests before handling them, so resending is safe. Vitest tests were added for the cache (csrf.test.ts) and for the assertion retry.

item.title: #3592276: Make preview drag and drop target the position under the cursor
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +258/−1 · js +258/−1
  • Diff: 7920a78
  • Discussion: #3592276 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Dragging a component in the Canvas editor preview now drops where the cursor is. Previously only a thin band at each component's top and bottom edge accepted drops, and a miss fell back to the drag label's rectangle, which sits 20px right of the cursor. Now every position over the previewed page shows an insertion indicator relative to the cursor. Releasing over the gray area outside the page no longer adds or moves a component. Layers panel drags are unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

customCollisionDetectionAlgorithm in the editor root now short-circuits for drags with origin overlay or library while the pointer is over the [data-canvas-editor-pane="true"] element. If the pointer is inside the .canvas--viewport-overlay, it calls the new findPreviewDropZoneId() in previewDropTarget.ts and returns the matching droppable as the only collision. Outside the page it returns no collisions, so a drop cancels. Other origins keep the existing rectIntersection or pointer-based logic.

findPreviewDropZoneId() reads the overlay DOM, not the drop zone rects. Starting at the root region, it descends into the child component under the pointer and then into that component's slot, until no slot is under the pointer. It stops descending when the pointer is within 12px of the component's edge, capped at a quarter of its size. That keeps it possible to drop beside a container whose slot fills it. In the chosen container it picks the nearest child and the before or after gap by the midpoint, along the stack direction. It maps the result to the existing drop zone ids (<uuid>_top, _bottom, _left, _right, or the slot or region id for an empty container), so the drop handling is untouched. It returns null when the drop would not move the dragged component.

To support this, the overlay components now emit data attributes: data-canvas-drop-item on ComponentOverlay, data-canvas-drop-container on RegionOverlay and SlotOverlay, and data-canvas-stack-direction on SlotOverlay. Unit tests cover the resolver.

item.title: #3592212: Config import blocked by in-use page-template components after upgrading Canvas from 1.10.1 to 1.12.0
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +141/−2 · php +141/−2
  • Diff: 6cbe297
  • Discussion: #3592212 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

A full config import could be refused with "Unable to import: the configuration change would delete the in-use Canvas component..." even though the exported component config was present. This happened when the same component (for example a page template or marker.page_content) had been created separately on each environment by an update, so the UUIDs differed. Config import now allows this case when the incoming component has the same source and still contains every version the existing one has. Imports that would drop the active version or a historical version are still blocked.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Core's storage comparer treats config with a different UUID as a delete plus a create under the same name. ComponentConfigImportValidator::onConfigImporterValidate() saw the delete and flagged the Component as in use. It now computes the intersection of the delete and create changelists to find recreated names. A recreated Component is no longer reported as endangered if the new private helper isRecreatedWithAllVersions() returns TRUE. That helper requires the incoming source to equal the active one and requires active_version to be set. Every version from the active Component::getVersions() must also appear in the incoming active_version or in the keys of versioned_properties (excluding VersionedConfigEntityBase::ACTIVE_VERSION). The reasoning is that content references Components by ID and version, not UUID. Tests cover recreating with and without the backing js_component also getting a new UUID. They also cover blocked imports when the active version or a historical version is missing.

item.title: #3592257: Support non-revisionable resources in Headless SDK draft mode
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +611/−12 · js +603/−12 · md +8
  • Diff: 7b4dfd4
  • Discussion: #3592257 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In Headless SDK draft mode, reading a single resource of a type without revisions, such as user--user, no longer fails. Drupal answered those reads with 501 Not Implemented, so single-resource reads could resolve to undefined and collection items silently fell back to published data. Non-revisionable resources are now readable in draft mode, and revisionable ones such as articles still return their working copy.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is in CanvasJsonApiClient in the drupal-canvas package. getResource() still adds the configured resource version (rel:working-copy) first. If Drupal replies with a JSON:API 501 error (status 501, JSON:API media type, an error with status: '501'), the client repeats the read once without the version. This applies only when the caller did not pick a version and did not request rawResponse.

The client remembers the type in a private unversionedTypes set only if the retry returns the requested resource (same type and id) with a links object that has no working-copy link. Drupal adds that link to every revisionable resource. After that, reads of the type skip the version parameter, and the result is cached under the unversioned key within the client's cache scope. If the retry looks different, for example an error, non-JSON, a collection, another id or a resource that has a working-copy link, the original 501 response is returned and nothing is cached or remembered. Network and draft-session errors still throw. getResourceByPath() goes through getResource(), so it gets the same behavior.

Collection reads now fetch a working copy only for items that carry a working-copy link (hasWorkingCopyLink()). Items of non-revisionable types are kept as they are, which avoids one failing request per item. The commit also adds a changeset marking this as a patch for drupal-canvas, plus tests.

item.title: #3592224: Allow component definition updates across headless frontends
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +506/−138 · js +268/−30 · mdx +174/−2 · php +64/−106
  • Diff: 3701415
  • Discussion: #3592224 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Headless frontends registered on one Canvas site (for example local, staging and production) can now provide the same component machine name with different definitions. Previously the sync rejected the second frontend with a conflict error. Now the most recent sync wins, and every frontend that synced the component keeps it in its own component list. After a sync that changes components, the open editor reloads its layout and drops cached props forms. The layer label and props form then match the preview, and newly added props appear without a browser reload. A new docs page, "Managing component changes", explains how definition changes reach pages and how to roll back.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In ExternalComponentSync, the guard that threw an UnexpectedValueException when another frontend owned the same external component with different metadata is removed, along with its helpers findConflictingOwningFrontend(), getConfiguredFrontends() and matchesExternalContract(). Components are shared by machine name, and the latest sync overwrites the label, status, props and slots. The kernel test shows that a changed definition creates a new Component version. Syncing the first frontend again reactivates its earlier version, and the other version stays loadable.

On the editor side, FrontendSelect now acts on the sync result. If created + updated > 0, it waits for pending preview requests and running componentAndLayoutApi queries and mutations. It then invalidates the Layout tag, invalidates a new ComponentInstanceForm tag (added to getComponentInstanceForm via providesTags), and dispatches setInitialized(false) and clearFieldValues(FORM_TYPES.COMPONENT_INSTANCE_FORM). It also clears the selected component, because the upgrade can remove it. The cached forms are dropped separately because metadata-only changes, such as prop titles, do not create a new component version. ComponentInstanceForm also now rebuilds its form query string when the selected node's type changes, which covers an instance upgraded to a new component version after a layout reload.

item.title: #3592221: Canvas AI: Show the selected component in the AI chat input
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +368/−38 · js +315/−38 · css +53
  • Diff: 8553fb0
  • Discussion: #3592221 · 1 contributor · 35 comments

Summary

In the Canvas AI dev chat (behind aiDevMode), selecting a single component now shows a chip at the top of the chat input box with the component's icon and name. Previously the agent received the selection but the chat gave no sign of it. A × button on the chip clears the selection. While an agent turn runs, the chip stays locked on the component that was selected when the message was sent, and its × is disabled. The live AiWizard.tsx is unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The chip is a new React component, SelectedComponentChip, rendered as a sibling of MemoDeepChat inside a position: relative Flex wrapper (.aiWizardChat). Deep-chat has no slot at the top of its input box, and passing selection state through deep-chat props would re-render it and wipe the live progress message. The chip reuses the preview's NameTag.module.css .nameTag class and Component1Icon. It subscribes to the selection itself via selectSelectedComponentUuid and selects only the node with findComponentByUuid, so layout edits during a turn do not re-render it. The × calls getDrupalSettings().canvas.componentSelectionUtils.unsetSelectedComponent() at click time, because that object is replaced on every render.

To keep the typed text below the chip, the chip toggles a data-has-selection attribute on the <deep-chat> host. A new :host([data-has-selection]) #text-input rule in DEEP_CHAT_AUXILIARY_STYLE then sets the top padding with !important, since deep-chat applies text padding inline. Input box size and chip offsets live in the new chatInputLayout.ts, so the two cannot drift apart. The chip stays on the box when the window is short.

In AiWizardDev.tsx, the isTurnInProgress boolean state became turnScope state ({ componentUuid }). It is set when the message is sent, using selectSelectedComponentUuid so only a single selection counts as scope. It is cleared when the turn ends. The activeComponentUuid sent to the backend is that same value, or ''. The Playwright test Page builder agent turns was extended to cover the hidden, shown, locked and deselect states. The test id is canvas-ai-selected-component.

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces feature branch, publishing a workspace through core (Workspaces UI, Drush, cron or $workspace->publish()) now handles Canvas drafts. Every pending Canvas item is validated and access checked first. If anything is invalid, the publish is refused with a message naming the items, and nothing goes live. If everything passes, config drafts (page variants, templates, code components and similar) are saved to Live together with the content revisions. Afterwards the workspace's Canvas draft storage is cleared. A published named workspace is deleted, and the Canvas default workspace is kept. There is no Canvas UI or API change.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New WorkspacePublishValidationException (carries getViolationSets()) thrown on pre-publish when Canvas drafts are invalid, plus the AutoSaveWorkspacePublishSubscriber event subscriber.

Technical details

The new AutoSaveWorkspacePublishSubscriber is registered with the event_subscriber tag in canvas.services.yml. It listens to WorkspacePrePublishEvent at priority -100, so it runs after other listeners such as content_moderation's. If an earlier listener already stopped the publish, it stages nothing. It listens to WorkspacePostPublishEvent at -600, after core's association cleanup.

Pre-publish runs inside executeInWorkspaceUnchecked() and walks AutoSaveManager::getAllAutoSaveList(). Each item gets an update access check. A Component generated from staged config is exempt, but only once discoveryReadsStagedConfig exists; that exemption is a todo for MR 4. Config items are validated through typed data. Content items get $entity->validate() plus the recorded form violations. A Page draft with an unresolved external-edit conflict is also refused, but only when canvas_dev_cd is installed. A content draft that storage rejected earlier (getRejectedDraftError()) blocks the publish until it is re-saved or discarded. Core has already captured the revisions to promote by then, so it can't be staged late.

Staged config translation overrides (StagedLanguageConfigOverride) are hidden from the item list. They get their own access and validation pass, and their base entity is validated from Live if it has no pending draft. If everything passes, WorkspaceAutoSave::stageFallbackDrafts() saves the fallback drafts to Live. Any draft that storage rejects is added as a violation. Failures throw the new WorkspacePublishValidationException, which core doesn't catch. Its message lists each item, because core's publish form and Drush only log getMessage().

Core dispatches the pre-publish event before opening its transaction, so these Live saves are not atomic with core's revision promotion. Only a publish driven by CanvasWorkspacePublisher, which is not in this change, can roll them back. A todo for MR 11 covers this. Access is checked as the current user, so Drush or cron publishes without update access are refused while the workspace holds Canvas drafts. Post-publish calls clearWorkspaceStores() and then deletes any workspace other than AutoSaveWorkspace::ID. A todo for MR 13 questions that delete, since core keeps a published workspace and the delete bypasses access checks. The PHPStan ignore for the previously unused stageFallbackDrafts() is removed, and todos for MR 14 mark the exception classes to move.

item.title: #3592176: Duplicating a page template silently does nothing: the GET representation is no longer a valid POST body
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592176 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The "Duplicate" action in the Templates panel (Page templates) now works. In Canvas 1.12.0 it appeared to do nothing, because the server rejected the request with a 422 and the UI hid the error. A copy of a disabled template now stays disabled, and any failure to duplicate is shown as an error card in the panel with a Dismiss button.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The GET representation of a page variant, since #3592106, includes the computed inputs_resolved and explicit null values for optional keys. buildDuplicateVariantPayload() in ui/src/services/pageVariants.ts spread each response item into the POST body, so POST /canvas/api/v0/config/page_variant failed validation. The fix is client-side only (the issue's Option A), so the server and the CLI, which reads inputs_resolved, are untouched. Each tree item is now rebuilt from storable keys: uuid, component_id, component_version, inputs, and parent_uuid, slot and label only when non-null. The status of the source is also carried over.

In ui/src/types/PageVariant.ts, a new PageVariantComponentTreeItemResponse type (nullable optional keys plus inputs_resolved) is used for PageVariant.component_tree. This way TypeScript rejects passing a read item where the write type PageVariantComponentTreeItem is expected. CreatePageVariantPayload gains an optional status. In PageVariants.tsx, handleDuplicate() now stores the rejection in duplicateError and renders an ErrorCard. The commit also adds a unit test and a Playwright test in pageVariants.spec.ts.

Summary

The Canvas AI get_component_details function, and get_component_context with catalog_only set to false, now describe multi-value props fully. Before, an array prop showed only type: array, so an AI agent could not tell what each value should be or how many values were allowed. In CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper, a new private getMultiValuePropMetadata() runs for props whose schema type is array. It adds items, normalized through propMetadataNormalizer with PropShape::normalizePropSchema() so format, contentMediaType and enum come through. It is now built from getJavaScriptComponent()->toSdcDefinition()['props']['properties'] and passed through componentPluginManager->resolveJsonSchemaReferences(), which keeps meta:enum. item.title: #3592216: Workspaces PR 2: hard dependency on core Workspaces, Main workspace, install and test scaffolding
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592216 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

This is the first MR of the Workspaces series on the 1.x-workspaces feature branch (planned in #3592187). Canvas now requires core Workspaces. Installing Canvas, or updating a 1.x site, enables workspaces and creates an undeletable "Main Canvas workspace" (canvas_default). Auto-save still uses the 1.x key-value store at the end of this MR, so editors see no change in how drafts are saved. The MR also adds ADR 0022, the design for staging Canvas drafts in workspaces, where the whole workspace is the unit of publish and per-item publish goes away. That ADR is marked "Proposed" and describes behaviour that later MRs in the series implement.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Core workspaces module becomes a required dependency of Canvas (core floor unchanged at ^11.3).
  • Database update: canvas_update_11201() (partial) enables workspaces and creates the Main workspace; Page owner and metatag fields become revisionable, with the update for existing sites in a later MR.
  • Config change: A canvas_default workspace ("Main Canvas workspace") is created on install/update and cannot be deleted while Canvas is installed.
  • New API: New Drupal\canvas\AutoSave\Workspace\AutoSaveWorkspace class with ID and LABEL constants.

Technical details

The Main workspace ID and label live in the new AutoSaveWorkspace class (ID = 'canvas_default'). WorkspaceAutoSaveRevisionHooks blocks deleting it: workspace_access forbids the delete operation, and workspace_predelete throws a LogicException for programmatic deletes. Per the issue description, the install and update code is canvas_install(), _canvas_ensure_auto_save_workspace() and a partial canvas_update_11201(). I could not read those files in the diff I received, so I have not checked them.

WorkspaceAutoSaveHooks::entityTypeBuild() assigns core's IgnoredWorkspaceHandler as the workspace handler on config entity types provided by canvas or a canvas_* module. Without it, core refuses to save those entities while a workspace is active.

Page now marks the owner field revisionable, and the metatag field on pages is also revisionable. A pending revision only carries revisionable fields, so this stops draft changes from skipping the draft and landing on the live page. The issue says an update for existing sites is planned as canvas_update_11202() in a later MR. ViewModeDisplayController now type-hints FormController instead of HtmlEntityFormController, because Workspaces decorates controller.entity_form. ApiConfigControllers, ApiContentControllers and ApiTranslationControllers gain a nullable WorkspaceManagerInterface $workspaceManager constructor argument, autowired from workspaces.manager. Per the comment in the diff, it is NULL while a 1.x site has not yet run canvas_update_11201(). It is not read yet: each is marked with a @todo Workspaces PR 5 and PHPStan ignores.

ComponentSourceManager takes a new TypedConfigManagerInterface and returns early from component generation when canvas.component_source_settings.* has no config schema. This covers the case where Canvas and Workspaces install in one batch and Layout Builder's cache tag invalidator clears the block manager before Canvas's schema is available. The workspace_switcher block is added to the excluded list in BlockComponentDiscovery. EntityFieldPropSourceMatcher skips fields that are explicitly internal, such as Workspaces' workspace revision field, using TypedDataHelper::isExplicitlyInternal().

Tests and docs make up the rest. The tests install workspaces, add the workspace cache context to expected responses, and add a WorkspacesDependencyUpdateTest update-path test. The docs are ADR 0022, docs/diagrams/workspace-autosave.md and a docs/personalization.md update. A @todo Workspaces PR convention is documented in the branch's PR-landing skill file.

Upgrade

Sites on Canvas 1.x updating to this branch should run database updates: per the issue, canvas_update_11201() enables workspaces and creates the canvas_default workspace. Core Workspaces is a core module, so there is no composer change, and the core floor stays ^11.3. Tests that install Canvas now also need workspaces and its schemas, a canvas_default workspace, and the workspace cache context in expected cache contexts. Controllers that read through controller.entity_form should type-hint Drupal\Core\Controller\FormController rather than HtmlEntityFormController.

item.title: #3592120: Canvas AI: Give the Canvas Agent editor-facing knowledge about Drupal Canvas
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592120 · 1 contributor · 20 comments

Summary

The Drupal Canvas Agent in the canvas_dev_ai module used to know only which Tool to select for a task and where the documentation lives. It could not answer questions like "How do I translate a page?" or "What is a page template?". Its prompt now includes editor-facing facts about the Canvas interface: pages, building a page, patterns, saving and publishing, page and content templates, translations, code components, and missing theme components. It is told to answer from those facts using the exact interface labels. When a question is not covered, it says so and points to https://project.pages.drupalcode.org/canvas/ instead of inventing an answer.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: modules/canvas_dev_ai/config/install/ai_agents.ai_agent.canvas_agent.yml has a rewritten system_prompt with editor-facing facts about Canvas.

Technical details

The change is confined to the system_prompt in modules/canvas_dev_ai/config/install/ai_agents.ai_agent.canvas_agent.yml. The prompt is restructured around two cases. Case A is a question, the default, answered only from a "Facts" section at the end of the prompt. Case B is a request to do the work, which the agent redirects to a Tool using the [canvas_dev_ai:available_tools] placeholder, with the existing Tool selection behaviour kept. Guardrails say never to add steps, labels, permissions, features or URLs that are not in the facts, to give only URLs that appear in the prompt, and to treat other Drupal or Canvas knowledge as unknown. Personalization, headless frontends, notifications and conflict resolution are explicitly declared out of scope, so the agent says so and gives the docs link. The facts were drafted by scanning the docs/ folder and the UI code with Claude, per the issue body, and then verified against the UI.

Upgrade

The prompt lives in config/install, so it applies on fresh installs of canvas_dev_ai. The issue says no update hook is added, so existing sites keep their stored canvas_agent config until it is reimported or re-saved.
